description: Cross-binding conformance for the INDEXED LHS spelling of an ARRAY-shaped observed (esm-spec §6.3.1). §6.3.1 admits TWO LHS spellings for the equation that DEFINES an unknown — bare (`y ~ f(…)`) and indexed (`y[i] ~ f(…)`, which defines the whole array `y`) — and neither is restricted by rank: the defining form is read through the LHS's BASE NAME, so "an arrayed definition is observed exactly as its scalar counterpart is". Julia's tree-walk build classified equations by the SYNTACTIC `lhs isa VarExpr`, so an array-shaped observed written the indexed way matched no owner bucket and was refused outright with `E_TREEWALK_UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE` on a document Rust and Python both loaded (issue #232). Every array observed in this fixture uses the indexed spelling and is asserted DIRECTLY — that is what makes the category state the §6.3.1 contract rather than the intersection the bindings happen to agree on; the states they drive are asserted alongside, so answering the observeds while dropping them out of the dynamics (or the reverse) still fails. The observeds are a CONTROLLED PAIR: `wf` is STATE-FREE and `ws` is STATE-DEPENDENT, the two classes a binding routes differently, so fixing one path only does not pass. Both right-hand sides are exactly integrable — D(u) = wf = 2k is a per-cell constant giving u[k](t) = 2*k*t, and D(v) = ws = 3*u is then linear in t giving v[k](t) = 3*k*t^2 — so every solver family named below reproduces the goldens to machine precision and a divergence here is a semantics divergence, never an integrator one. PYTHON IS EXPECTED TO FAIL THIS CATEGORY TODAY and is kept in bindings_required on purpose (it has a real runner, so scope_excluded would be the wrong mechanism): it answers 0.0 for both indexed-LHS observeds. See README.md and CONFORMANCE_SPEC §5.30.1 for the three divergences and PR #237, which carries the Python fixes — measured, not assumed: #237 at head 67504523 closes none of the three, scoring the same 7/13 as main. Julia is the reference binding: its `run_pde_tests` minted golden/observed_indexed_lhs.json.
